$\text{Slope}=\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}=\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}$

We can calculate the change in $x$ and change in $y$ by picking any two pairs of corresponding $x$- and $y$-values.

$\begin{array}{lrrrr}
&&\xrightarrow{+1}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+1}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+1}\,\,\,\,
\\
x
&12
&13
&14
&15
\\
\hline
\\
y
&-4
&2
&8
&14
\\
&&\xrightarrow[+6]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[+6]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[+6]{}\,\,\,\,
\end{array}$

So the slope is:

$\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}=\dfrac{6}{1}=6$
